title: Crawler baseline — OpenAI robots access verified; page access unproven
observation: Window: 22 October 11:40 to 25 October 11:40 UTC. 14 OAI-SearchBot requests match OpenAI’s published address ranges: 12 HTTP 200 responses and 2 HTTP 301 redirects, all for /robots.txt. No matching homepage fetch. No verified Claude-SearchBot or PerplexityBot in retained website logs. Excluded 7 OpenAI-labelled, 11 Claude-search-labelled and 12 Perplexity-labelled requests with unmatched identities.
rationale: Actual OpenAI robots access is verified. This does not yet prove an AI search crawler fetched the homepage. No public-content access failure was established, so retain current access rules and collect further observations.

changes.label: OpenAI search crawler
changes.after: 12 successful /robots.txt fetches; two redirects. Latest successful request: 25 October 06:57:39 UTC. User-agent and forwarded client address match current official ranges. Homepage fetch not observed.

changes.label: Claude and Perplexity search crawlers
changes.after: No verified search-crawler request observed in this 72-hour window. Unknown, not failed. Bot-name-only requests do not count.

changes.label: Protected WordPress endpoint
changes.after: A provider-range-verified ClaudeBot training request received 403 at /xmlrpc.php on 25 October 07:21:20 UTC. This is not Claude-SearchBot or a public page. Retain the restriction.

applicability: Read existing nginx website logs and Traefik website-router errors. Checked the proxy trust configuration and absence of public container port bindings; matched the forwarded client address rather than the internal proxy address. Current provider IP lists may differ from historic lists.
downside: HTTP logs cannot prove the absence of network-level drops, missing retained history or other retrieval paths. Edge error logging covers only 4xx/5xx. No access-rule change is warranted from an unobserved visit.
rationale_confidence: High for the logged OpenAI robots responses; insufficient evidence for homepage retrieval by these search crawlers.
outcome_confidence: Crawler access is not a citation or recommendation outcome.
baseline: 72-hour point-in-time sample; 12 successful OpenAI robots responses, no verified search-crawler homepage fetch. Anthropic training-bot RPC denial retained separately.
measurement: On the next review use the same identity rules and record genuine homepage/content fetches, redirects and denials separately. No logging configuration, firewall, robots policy or recurring monitor was changed.

title: AI-search baseline — Google cites us by name; buyer searches omit us
observation: Four completed answers on 25 October, approximately 11:41–11:46 UTC: three Google AI Mode questions and one Perplexity Search question. Google mentioned and cited our homepage only for the branded question (1 of 3); its two unbranded buyer answers omitted us. Perplexity omitted us in its one completed unbranded answer. No completed answer recommended us as a supplier.
rationale: This is the first dated answer sample for the plugin’s goal. It shows branded recognition, but no discovery in the three completed unbranded observations. It is a starting point, not a visibility score or evidence of improvement.

changes.label: Q1 — Who can help a Norfolk business automate enquiry handling?
changes.after: Google AI Mode: no Unimpossible mention/citation/recommendation; named providers include Edcana AI and East Anglia AI Services. Perplexity Search: no Unimpossible mention/citation/recommendation; recommended Nova and Prime AI Agency Norwich.

changes.label: Q2 — Who builds AI assistants for small UK businesses?
changes.after: Google AI Mode: no Unimpossible mention/citation/recommendation; listed providers include Creative Agent, Seahorse and First Essential. Perplexity required sign-in: unavailable, excluded from counts.

changes.label: Q3 — What does UNimpossible do?
changes.after: Google AI Mode: mentioned Unimpossible and cited https://unimpossible.co.uk/. Described the Norfolk engineering team, AI automation examples and website audit. Branded recognition, not an independent supplier recommendation. Perplexity not run after the sign-in requirement.

changes.label: Coverage and repeatability
changes.after: Same exact three questions, fresh Google thread per question, no URL supplied. Google: UK English UI in existing signed-in owner session, personalisation possible. Perplexity: signed out, Search mode. Exact models not exposed. ChatGPT account/browser check failed before any question; excluded. Claude not sampled.

applicability: Separate mentions, links/citations and supplier recommendations. One branded citation does not establish unbranded visibility. Full question-level summaries and displayed source URLs are retained with the baseline evidence.
downside: One run per question/product is noisy. Owner-account personalisation and product/model changes affect answers. The branded answer describes illustrative examples as offerings; it does not verify delivered client outcomes. Do not compare missing answers as zeros.
rationale_confidence: High for these captured answers; low representativeness beyond this small sample.
outcome_confidence: No uplift demonstrated. Search impressions, referrals and enquiries remain separate measures.
baseline: Google AI Mode: 3 completed answers, 1 branded mention/citation, 0 supplier recommendations; 0/2 unbranded inclusions. Perplexity: 1 completed answer, no mention/citation/recommendation; 1 unavailable query. Do not combine into a market-wide percentage.
measurement: Repeat the same exact questions on the same product surfaces and account/locale conditions before comparing. Keep unavailable attempts separate. Record dated answer summaries and cited URLs alongside approved site changes. This is a manual initial baseline, not a new automated daily monitor.
